meta.purpose: Policy-exposure matrix replacing crude party-label baskets. Each ticker scored on concrete policy transmission channels so market moves can be tested against policy exposure rather than donor identity.
meta.scoring: Each dimension -3..+3. Positive = benefits from Democratic policy direction (subsidy expansion, regulation, rate cuts, wealth-tax redistribution). Negative = benefits from Republican direction (deregulation, fossil expansion, crypto-light-touch, defense buildup).
meta.caveat: Scores are analyst judgement, not measured data. They are hypotheses to be tested against price action, not facts.

dimensions.subsidy: Dependence on federal subsidy / tax credit (IRA, CHIPS, farm bill). Positive = needs subsidy to earn.
dimensions.govContract: Dependence on federal contracts (defense, detention, healthcare reimbursement). Positive = benefits from expanded federal spending.
dimensions.regulation: Direction of regulatory pressure. Positive = benefits from MORE regulation (compliance moat, competitor burden). Negative = would be hurt by more regulation.
dimensions.rates: Duration sensitivity. Positive = long-duration, benefits from rate cuts. Negative = benefits from higher rates (banks NIM).
dimensions.wealthTax: Exposure to wealth tax / capital gains / mark-to-market proposals. Positive = would likely BENEFIT from redistribution (lower-end consumption). Negative = would be directly hit.
dimensions.crypto: Crypto regulatory friendliness. Positive = benefits from permissive crypto regime.
dimensions.tariff: Tariff / trade-policy exposure. Positive = benefits from tariffs on imports (domestic producers). Negative = hurt by tariffs (import-dependent).
